en.name: Immaculate Conception
en.summary: The feast marking the dogma that Mary was conceived free from original sin.
en.body: The Immaculate Conception celebrates the belief that Mary, from the very moment of her conception, was preserved free from original sin in anticipation of her role as the mother of Jesus. Devotion to the idea developed over many centuries before Pope Pius IX formally defined it as dogma in 1854. It is the patronal feast of the United States and falls during Advent, nine months before the feast of Mary's birth.
